what.text: This page follows Venezuelans in Aruba whom UNHCR counts as other people in need of international protection, a group separate from refugees.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 11470 people in this group in Aruba, 0.2% of all Venezuelans in it.
The largest numbers of Venezuelan refugees live in Spain, Brazil, the United States and Mexico.

why.text: The fact pack records no armed conflict and no dated events for Venezuela, so it does not say why people left.
The main years of displacement in the data run from 2018 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR has counted this group only since 2018, and the figure reached its highest point, 17085, at the end of 2023.
It was lower at the end of 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in Aruba.
These are year-end totals for Aruba only, and the group is never added to refugees.
